newsitem.title: POLAND: BRE wants its warrants traded on bourse.
newsitem.headline: BRE wants its warrants traded on bourse.

text.p: Polish Bank Rozwoju Exportu wants its warrants, so far only privately placed, to be soon traded on the Warsaw bourse, the bank's deputy president said on Wednesday.
"We have started work to introduce our warrants to the Warsaw bourse, but I can not say how long it will take," Wojciech Kostrzewa told a news conference.

There are no derivative instruments traded on the Warsaw stock exchange so far, but Kostrzewa expected the bourse would be keen to start listing them soon because of competition in that sector from the Vienna bourse.

BRE has so far issued call warrants for non-public trade on seven Polish stocks, mostly blue chips with big shares in market turnover and traded in the continuous system, on mass privatisation units (PSU), treasury bonds and T-bills.

Despite growing interest from companies and institutional investors, warrants have been so far bought mostly by large private investors, because accounting methods for such instruments have not yet been set.

Konrad Szwedowski, head of the bank's capital markets department, said that even though short-selling of securities was already legally possible, the bank would wait until such transactions become popular before offering put warrants to clients.
